digest.component_or_area: tracker initialization and environment identity management
propositions: Re-cloning a tracker without carrying over .env-id causes the system to mint a new environment identity with no warning, silently invalidating all attestations signed by the prior environment.
init._ensure_env_id_unit and init._gen_local_files mint a fresh uuid whenever .env-id is absent without checking whether the store already holds events from a different environment.

Minting .env-id into a store containing another environment's events must warn loudly on stderr, name the prior env id(s), state the attestation consequence, and require REBAR_ALLOW_ENV_REIDENTIFY=1 to proceed.

rebar fsck must emit a counted ENV_ID_MISMATCH issue (scoped by author) when the current environment's own author also wrote events under a different env id, detecting store-wide re-identification problems at scan time rather than discovery at a gate.
Multi-clone topology where different authors write under different env ids must not trigger ENV_ID_MISMATCH, only re-identification by the same author.

docs/concurrency.md must document the git-ignored local state carry-over list (.env-id, .opcert-key, .opcert-key.pub, .ensure-applied), what breaks per file, and why the guard warns rather than refuses.
